finding: DSK no longer publishes the fixed-asset renewal, disposal and depreciation tables by branch, nor the capital-yield index
evidence: 6 URLs (017_2en.xls, 017_3en.xls, 017_4en.xls, 017_5en.xls, 017_6en.xls, 017_7en.xls) return an HTML page with HTTP 200; the section is commented out of the DSK industry index and file numbers 017_1/018_1/018_2 now hold regional product tables
consequence: Renewal and depreciation rates by branch are NOT AVAILABLE; FR10 uses the investment rate (I/GO, DSK 019) and the national-accounts consumption of fixed capital and fixed assets by section (DSK NA 013, 031) as alternatives (gaps table)

finding: The workbook's 2025 branch columns are a different (preliminary) vintage from DSK
evidence: workbook industry total 63,123 vs DSK 63,011 mn AZN (+0.18%); largest branch gaps: Machinery and equipment +228%, Fabricated metal products -40%, Basic metals -20%, Other transport equipment -12%; 2016-2024 agree to 0.000%
consequence: FR10 takes 2025 branch data from DSK; the workbook branch rows are used only where they match DSK

finding: Branch investment does not add up to the industry total before 2010
evidence: unattributed investment -3.05% to -0.41% of the total in 2005-2009; exact (<0.01%) from 2010; mining-support investment printed as "-" until 2017 although its output was 1,342 mn AZN a year
consequence: Investment rates are used from 2010 in the determinants panel; mining-support investment before 2018 is treated as missing, not zero

finding: Volume indices printed in thousands of per cent with a "t." suffix
evidence: DSK 009 prints e.g. "7.8 t." (= 7 800% of 2010) in 48 cells of sheet 9.2 and 4 of sheet 9.1; read naively these cells become missing
consequence: to_num reads the suffix (Part 2); real output is chained from 9.1 (previous year = 100) only

finding: National-accounts income account does not close by section in 2016
evidence: VA - compensation - other taxes - GOS = C -22.5, D +7.3, E +15.2 mn AZN in 2016 (sum -0.00); exact in every other year
consequence: An allocation error between sections C, D, E; GOS margins of those sections in 2016 are uncertain by these amounts

finding: Water supply runs a negative gross operating surplus; the income-account total row carries the section code "C"
evidence: section E GOS -155.7 mn AZN in 2025 (compensation 454.3 > value added 301.7); negative in 5 of 21 years
consequence: Not an error but an economic fact (a subsidised utility); the total row is identified by its label, not its code

finding: The DVX "rentabellik" (profitability) row is a tax ratio, not profitability
evidence: r223 equals payable profit tax / income after deductions to 0.05 pp in every year 2021-2025 (2.2-2.8%); the profitability the declarations imply, (income after deductions - deductible expenses) / deductible expenses, is 10.0-13.2%; taxable profit minus declared loss equals that net result to 7.60 mn AZN
consequence: FR10 reports the declaration margin computed from the components and labels r223 as an effective tax ratio

finding: DVX budget-organisation rows duplicate the micro-taxpayer rows; micro-taxpayer count carries a money unit
evidence: rows 127-129 equal rows 123-125 in every year: True; row 123 (a count) is labelled "mln. manat"
consequence: Budget-organisation taxpayer counts are NOT AVAILABLE; the size-class table uses the micro rows only (as FR4 F4)

finding: DVX taxpayer counts carry a population unit
evidence: rows 111, 115 and 119 (numbers of large, medium and small taxpayers, e.g. 846 large payers in 2022) are labelled "min nəfər" (thousand persons)
consequence: Read as counts of taxpayers; the unit should be corrected in the workbook

finding: Regional industrial output does not add up to the national total before 2019, and includes household industry after
evidence: sum of 14 regions vs DSK 010: -13.9% to -1.7% in 2003-2018, exact from 2019; DSK 022 footnotes 2019+ as "considering industrial activities of households and informal individual owners"
consequence: Regional shares are modelled on the regional sum (shares add to one by construction); the 2018/2019 change of coverage is a level break, handled by a step dummy in the regional share equations

finding: FR1's 2024 section value added is an earlier vintage than DSK's
evidence: FR1 manufacturing VA 2024 7,475.5 vs DSK NA 7,019.4 mn AZN (+6.5%); the two agree exactly in 2025
consequence: FR10 anchors on 2025, where FR1 and DSK coincide, and uses FR1 only as growth indices from 2025

finding: SME indicators exist for two years only; the statistical register is a single snapshot
evidence: DSK entrepreneurship tables cover 2023 and 2024; st_units tables are as of 1 July 2026 (entry/exit January-June 2026)
consequence: SME shares and register-based entry/exit rates are presented, not modelled: no time series exists to identify a projection

finding: The published non-state share of industry is inconsistent with its own branch breakdown in some years
evidence: output-weighted branch non-state shares (DSK 010_2 x 010) differ from the published industry total by 2005 -0.8 pp, 2013 +6.3 pp, 2014 +7.6 pp, 2015 +7.9 pp, 2016 +6.7 pp; within 0.15 pp in every other year
consequence: The forecast of the non-state share is built from the branch composition (consistent by construction); the published total for those years should be queried with DSK

finding: FR3's branch wage paths are not anchored on 2025 branch wages and share one growth rate
evidence: FR3 2026 branch wage / DSK 2025 branch wage - 1 ranges -21% to +21% across 29 branches; 2026-2030 growth is 7.72-7.72% a year for every branch
consequence: FR10 applies FR1's average-wage index to each branch's 2025 DSK wage; FR3 is not used for levels
